lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: CarMax's own ABS servicer reports through August 2026 show no new credit deterioration in the securitised Tier 1 book, which the 10-Q puts at 95.6% of the portfolio. The 2025-3 trust at 13 months (31+ day delinquency 1.75%, cumulative net loss 0.49%) tracks 2024-3 at the same age a year earlier (1.63%, 0.60%). The problem 2023 vintage (trust 2023-4) deteriorated April to August 2026 by +1.22pp of delinquency, against +1.11pp over the same months of 2025, and its cumulative net loss accrual slowed. So a repeat of Q2 FY26's $71.3m reserve build for the 2022-2023 vintages looks unlikely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has been the downside line. Q2 FY26 (2025-09-25) fell 20.07% on a $142.2m provision that included the $71.3m vintage build (https://investors.carmax.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2025/CarMax-Reports-Second-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results/default.aspx). Q1 FY27 (2026-06-17) fell 8.98% partly on CAF credit worry about Tier 2 expansion, even though the provision fell to $95.6m. The market punishes credit surprises. The absence of one has not been shown to pay.

findings.finding: The revenue bar of $6.94bn (+5.3% YoY) implies roughly flat retail units against a Q2 FY26 comparison of -6.3% comps. Management blamed that quarter on demand pulled into Q1 by tariffs and on price competitiveness hurt by depreciation. Q1 FY27 ran a two-year comp stack of +7.3% (+8.1% then -0.8%). Cox says used retail sales strengthened through August, with retail days' supply falling from 46 to 44, so units and revenue probably clear the bar by about 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not paid. Q1 FY27 beat revenue by about 8% ($8.01bn against ~$7.39bn) and EPS by 36%, and the stock fell 8.98% (https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/06/17/carmax-kmx-q1-earnings.html). Only 2 of the last 8 prints rose (+6.59% on 2025-06-20, when Q1 FY26 comps were +8.1%, and +3.45%).

findings.finding: Wholesale values fell about 2.2% during the quarter (Manheim index 212.9 in June, ~209.8 in July, 208.2 in August 2026). Cox called the August decline 'more than typical'. On the index's own year-over-year figures, the same window in 2025 fell only about 0.5%. Depreciation within the quarter is the mechanism CarMax itself blamed for lost price competitiveness in Q2 FY26, so it pressures wholesale GPU (Q2 FY26: $993) and possibly retail GPU beyond the ~$200 guided decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GPU compression drove the June 2026 sell-off (-8.98%; retail GPU -$230 to $2,177) and the April 2026 sell-off (-15.12%; GPU -$207 to $2,115, https://investors.carmax.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/CarMax-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2026-Results/default.aspx). findings.finding: The Q4/FY guide will be struck at spot fuel with Brent at ~$106 on 2026-09-28 against a June basis equivalent to ~$80 Brent for Q4 (March assumption, unchanged in June to within $0.01), a ~30%+ rise that on the company's own sensitivity (~$46m of Q4 net income per 10%, derived from $102m remainder-of-year less $56m Q3) is ~$0.10-0.13 of Q4 EPS — deeper than the $0.07 Q4 cut BofA made (to $0.20), so the Q4 guide risks printing below the Street's Q4 number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line this stock trades on: June 2026 beat on EPS and fell 4.87% (baseline) / -5.75% premarket on the yield-guide cut to 2.25% from 3.25%; Dec 2025 raised outlook +9.8%.

findings.finding: The June 30 2026 annual goodwill test is likely to produce an impairment. At FY25 the single CGU had only $34.2m of headroom on a $254.2m carrying value, and the company disclosed that a 10% change in the exit EV/revenue multiple moves fair value by about $22m. FY26 EBITDA guidance has since been cut from 17-19% to 15-16%, and equity of $248.4m at 2026-03-31 compares with a market cap near US$118m. Yet the Q3 interim statements say 'has not identified any indicators of impairment'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior impairment: FY25 recognised none, per the 40-F statements. No history on this line.

findings.finding: Freight costs kept rising after the May 13 guide. Asia to US West Coast spot rates were $3,624/FEU in late May, up 74% on late February, and the June Hormuz reopening broke down in early July. That bears on the product and fulfilment cost the company itself blamed for the margin cut, and it is a risk to the low end of Q4 EBITDA and to the first half of the FY27 margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-line surprises on confirmed prints: -13.72% on 2025-09-17 (the FY26 initial guide below FY25 like-for-like) and -10.51% on 2026-05-13 (the margin cut). Both are US-line moves in a name trading about 7k shares a day there.

lessons_applied: Impairment cut from -0.5 to -0.3 and kept as one_off. Lesson 2's reported-quarter exception covers a quantified impairment, and the 'what has worked' section covers a documented one. Shipping cut from -0.4 to -0.2. Lesson 5 treats the post-guide worsening as macro-to-company transmission with no company confirmation. Lesson 9 requires sizing net of the roughly 60% software and the growing infrastructure segments.

findings.finding: Q3 FY26 (10-Q) opex was $40.8M: mineral property expenditures $29.5M, up from $15.7M, and G&A $9.4M. The Wyoming/Texas workforce went from 103 to 185 and construction is done in-house. Interest income was $4.2M. Q3's pre-mark loss was about $33M ($0.068/share on ~491M weighted shares); the other $0.04 of the -$0.11 was a $19.4M fair-value loss. If opex holds, the $9M consensus revenue at a ~$51/lb purchased-inventory cost basis ($73.9M / 1.456M lb) adds only ~$3.5M of gross profit. That puts Q4 near -$0.06 before marks, against a -$0.04 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print (2026-06-09 amc) missed EPS at -$0.11 vs -$0.03 with zero revenue: -11.55% (baseline; https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/06/53082430/uranium-energy-reports-q3-results-with-wider-eps-loss-shares-slide). The 2026-03-10 print was in line on EPS with about 2x the revenue estimate and moved -2.28% (baseline). Misses get sold and beats do not get bought. Zacks puts the average EPS surprise at -18%, so misses are habitual.

findings.finding: Revenue depends on a discretionary sale from inventory, and the tape was against one. On the Q3 call management said it 'preserved our inventory' in flat prices, when the April-end mark was about $87/lb ($127M / 1.456M lb). Zacks puts the May-July spot average at $85.19/lb, below that level and far below the $101/lb of the Q2 sale. A second zero-revenue quarter against the $9M bar is a live outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Zero revenue in Q3 FY26 (together with the EPS miss): -11.55%. Revenue about 2x the estimate in Q2 FY26 ($20.2M from 200k lb at $101): -2.28% (baseline; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/uranium-energy-corp-reports-results-for-second-quarter-of-fiscal-2026-302708835.html).

outside_window.finding: The UR&C conversion facility's Class 4 cost study, and with it site selection, was guided on the Q3 call to the first half of calendar 2027. That caps how far a refinery headline on 09-29 can go beyond naming a site.

lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning): both findings are negatives against a -10.7 call skew and ~14% short interest at a 52-week low. Shrank F1 from -1.0 to -0.6 and F2 from -0.5 to -0.3, and the expected move from -0.6 to -0.3.
